niche: night-time economy hotspot patrol slate off offences the force records as an occurrence window rather than a time, the window being the gap in the target keeper's own routine
answer: Commission Thursday 20:00 to 00:00, Saturday 00:00 to 04:00, Sunday 00:00 to 04:00, Sunday 20:00 to 00:00, Friday 12:00 to 16:00, Wednesday 20:00 to 00:00, Monday 20:00 to 00:00 and Tuesday 20:00 to 00:00, covering 5,700 covered offences a season (5,705.20 unrounded), with Friday 16:00 to 20:00 the runner-up at 400.
stakeholder_role: community safety manager of a city partnership, who commissions the 2027 hotspot patrol slate

spine.row_meaning: one recorded offence, with the earliest and the latest time it can have occurred

world.geography: Kelverstoke, a fictional city in a UK-like island state

layer1: offence records whose occurrence time is a window (occurred_from and occurred_to) and whose report time is a third timestamp
two recording systems across the window, the force's legacy incident export to March 2026 and the new records management system after it, with different column names and time formats
the same offence present in both exports across the cut-over fortnight under two reference numbers
a licensed premises register whose addresses match the offence locations only through a gazetteer with two spellings per street
night-time economy footfall counts from four pedestrian sensors with gaps where a sensor was down
a patrol tasking plan in a spreadsheet, one sheet per quarter, hours written as text
offences recorded under a British Summer Time local clock across two clock changes
an offence class whose counts jump when a national counting rule changed, documented in the extract notes
driver: The decisive quantity is a latent cyclical profile recovered from records that observe each event only as the interval it fell in, where the interval is the gap in the target's own inspection routine and its length varies systematically with the part of the cycle it covers, so the flat reading that spreads each event evenly across its own interval divides the busiest parts of the cycle across the longest intervals and the quietest across the shortest, and only the placement under which the recorded intervals are the likeliest set to have been recorded recovers the profile.
driver_concrete: A covered offence is against a target its keeper looks at on a routine, so the record's window is the gap in that routine, and the gap covering a Friday or Saturday night is a weekend closure of 39 to 64 hours against a midweek night's 14 to 16. Spreading each window evenly over its own hours, which is the textbook aoristic weight, writes the quarter's heaviest nights down and its daytime absences up and moves the patrol slate onto Friday afternoon; the hour-of-week clock the record settles puts it back on the evenings and the small hours.
stump: The default path spreads each occurrence window evenly over its own hours and commissions Friday 12:00 to 16:00, Thursday 20:00 to 00:00, Friday 00:00 to 04:00, Saturday 00:00 to 04:00, Friday 16:00 to 20:00, Thursday 16:00 to 20:00, Friday 20:00 to 00:00 and Sunday 20:00 to 00:00, filing 3,150 covered offences a season, when its eight meet only 4,250 of the golden's 5,700; the step that lands it there is reading the window as a claim that the offence is equally likely in each of its hours, when the window is the keeper's own closure and the closures covering the heaviest nights are the longest.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every column correctly, conforms the legacy export to the new records management export, drops the cross-system duplicates, fixes the gazetteer and keeps the contracted classes takes the textbook aoristic weight, spreading each window evenly over its own hours, and files the slate led by Friday 12:00 to 16:00 at 3,150 covered offences a season. Executed on the generator's clean truth in checks.py, which asserts that slate, its figure, and that its eight meet at most 0.80 of the golden's coverage.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the quarter's hour-of-week offence clock for the contracted classes, and the field's own method is aoristic crime analysis read as what it is, an interval-censored observation of a time: the clock the record settles is the one under which the recorded windows are the likeliest set to have been recorded, and the record refutes the flat start at a likelihood ratio of 3,035.2. Swap the nouns for a depot's relief crew and breakdowns and there is no keeper routine, so no window and no closure-length variation, and nothing is left to recover.

differentiation.task180: t180 distorts the hourly profile by the instruments' sensitivity following a daily cycle, so small events are missing from the record; here every event is in the record and it is the precision of its time that varies, so the distortion is in where the recorded events are placed, not in which are recorded.
differentiation.task464: task464 converts one instrument's scale to another's by matching the two distributions in a sample measured on both, so its decisive step is a conversion between two measured scales and both scales are observed. Here nothing is measured twice: no covered offence's time is observed at all for four in five of them, and the decisive step recovers an unobserved hour-of-week clock from the overlap of interval-censored windows, with the record's own likelihood refuting every alternative placement (the even spread at 3,035.2, the keeper-seen offences' profile at 13,660.0, the witnessed classes' hours at 3,435.4 and footfall at 7,834.8).

Shipped 10-12 as the single-layer version and left off the portal's approved list.
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is what a shared resource adds to a site, and both arms of that difference are taken from the site's own filed plan when the site's records show it never meets the plan: the untreated arm has to be read from what the site does on its own, and the shortfall its treated periods show against the plan has to be split into the part the resource caused and the part that was there anyway, so subtracting the whole shortfall while keeping the plan as the untreated arm, the obvious correction, ranks the sites wrongly too.
lineage.stump: A competent solver runs the planning standard on each airport's 2027 design days and summer roster pattern with the unit's three lanes added and posts the unit to Cullinvale (697,500 passengers moved within the standard); the step that lands it there is taking the roster pattern as the lanes that will be open on both arms of the comparison, when the checkpoints' own lane counts show seven of the eight opening fewer lanes at their banks than the pattern plans on every day of the summer, Eskerford two fewer, so the posting moves the most at Eskerford (342,200).
lineage.niche: posting a national screening agency's one mobile screening unit to one of eight flagged airports for the summer, judged by the passengers it moves within the 20-minute queue standard, when host airports stand down their own lanes while the unit is there
lineage.answer: Post the mobile screening unit to Eskerford from 15 June to 31 August 2027: it moves 342,200 passengers within the 20-minute standard, against 272,600 at Halloran Bay, and 13 per cent is the smallest whole per cent shortfall in Eskerford's forecast passengers at which another posting would move more.
